article_title: The Shwegugyi Pagoda Inscription, Pagan, 1141 A.D.
translation_text: Reverence to the Buddha, whose pure mind / Made for the earth a Sun-his noble Law, / That all three worlds may follow him and reach / Salvation, who were powerless else to cross / The jungle and slough of sensuality. / To the sole Lord I bow, His Law, His Church.
notes: Dry-run extraction of the first published translation unit only. This is copied from the OCRed JBRS article rather than newly translated.

article_title: Ananda Brick Monastery Inscriptions of Pagan
translation_text: Homage to the Omniscient One! May this Brick Monastery remain long! This Brick Monastery was caused to be erected on Friday the 15th and fullmoon day of the bright half of the month of the lunar mansion Puṣya (Dec.-Jan.) in the year 2319 of the Sāsana Era, post-Parinibbāna of the Conqueror of the fivefold Māra, or in the year 1137 of the Kali Yuga (A.D. 1775), having purchased 450,000 bricks for 1,800 coins and having paid 50 coins to carriers of red ochre and water and 600 coins to master brick-masons. By whom was it caused to be erected? by a lay devotee, Utthanarājā by name ... For the benefit of being free from the threefold cycles of birth and for the benefit of realising nibbāna ... this Brick Monastery was caused to be erected. On Sunday the 4th day of the dark half of the month of Pūrvaphalguṇa (Aug.-Sept.) in the year 1141 of the Kali Yuga (A.D. 1779), this monastery was completed.
notes: First Burmese-relevant dry-run extraction for Ananda. The published translation is P1-centred on pages 6-7, and the linked source unit records the mixed B1/P2/B2 witness notes preserved later in the article rather than inventing a new source transcription.
